name: Alpine APK
protocol: APK v2 package/index format consumed by apk-tools bundled with Alpine 3.24.2; v3 wire format is a separate future capability.
publish: Admin ingestion of .apk files with architecture/channel metadata; generate and sign APKINDEX generations with the feed key. Package bytes/signatures are preserved.
read: apk update/add/fetch from local, remote-cached or replica channels; architecture paths remain explicit.
special: Import trusted verification keys explicitly. Remote signed indexes are preserved; a composed local repository requires explicit regeneration and its own signing identity. Do not silently extend metadata expiry.
excluded: No APK v3 wire-format generation claim; no operating-system image build or package compilation.
scenarios: Publish two architectures; apk update/add selects the correct package and verifies signatures.
Corrupt index/signature is rejected; stale remote bytes never masquerade as newly signed metadata.

name: Ansible Galaxy
protocol: Galaxy collection API v3 with API-root discovery and asynchronous import status.
publish: ansible-galaxy collection publish uploads a built collection; validate namespace/name/version, archive inventory and dependencies; expose import status until commit.
read: Collection version discovery, dependency resolution and archive delivery for ansible-galaxy collection install; local/remote/replica sources.
special: Use a scoped Galaxy API token. Resolve download URLs through authorized source mappings; cancellation or failed import leaves no installable version.
excluded: Legacy Galaxy roles, web-community/social APIs and executing collection code during ingestion are excluded.
scenarios: Publish a collection with a dependency, wait for import, install via one configured server.
Invalid archive or unauthorized namespace fails import; a cancelled import is not advertised.

name: APT / Debian
protocol: Debian dists/pool repository layout with InRelease, Release/Release.gpg, Packages/Sources and SHA-256 by-hash.
publish: Admin ingestion of .deb and source bundles (.dsc and referenced files) into distribution/component/architecture; publish one signed index generation.
read: apt update/install and apt source using local or byte-preserving remote/replica snapshots; support compressed index representations.
special: Keep by-hash generations reachable while readers complete. Remote trust and local signing keys are distinct. Source bundle references must be complete before publishing.
excluded: No arbitrary union of independently signed Release trees; translations/Contents generation and distro build-farm orchestration are not required initial workflows.
scenarios: Ingest package/source bundle; update/install/source with trusted signing key and by-hash.
Index update during concurrent download cannot yield hash-sum mismatch; tampered or expired metadata fails.

name: CocoaPods
protocol: HTTP CDN-style podspec discovery and pod source/archive delivery for CocoaPods 1.17.0.
publish: Admin ingestion of validated podspec JSON plus an immutable source archive or explicit external source reference; regenerate CDN metadata atomically.
read: pod install/update resolves specs and downloads declared source archives; support local, remote CDN cache and replica feeds.
special: Keep source hashes and podspec version identity. Full offline seed must materialize referenced source archives; VCS-only references are visibly external and block a complete-offline claim.
excluded: No CocoaPods Trunk account/API clone, general Git hosting or pod repo push endpoint. Publication uses documented admin ingestion; CDN consumption remains a real-client workflow.
scenarios: Ingest podspec/archive; pod install on macOS fetches the selected version from the feed.
Conflicting pod version or mismatched archive hash fails; a source-only external dependency is reported in seed preflight.

name: Composer / PHP
protocol: Composer 2 repository packages.json and per-package metadata-url, dist archives and source references.
publish: Admin ingestion of composer package metadata and dist archives; validate name/version/dependency metadata and checksums. Native Composer has no registry publish command requirement here.
read: composer install/update with dist delivery and explicit source references through local/remote/replica feeds.
special: Rewrite permitted dist URLs to authorized immutable assets; preserve external VCS references as external. A full offline replica requires a usable dist closure. Generated metadata is coherent per package.
excluded: Composer 1 provider-index compatibility and acting as a general VCS server are excluded initially.
scenarios: Install a locked dependency set from a locally ingested dist and repeat offline from a seeded replica.
A duplicate private name never falls through to a public upstream; missing dist closure prevents full-offline completion.

name: Conan
protocol: Conan 2 remote API with recipe revisions, package IDs and package revisions.
publish: conan upload publishes recipes and binary packages with revisions/manifests; validate referenced files and immutable revision identity.
read: conan list/install/download resolves revision-aware recipes and binaries via local, remote cache and replica.
special: Preserve revision chronology for latest resolution; auth tokens map to shared scopes. Retention cannot drop recipe/manifests needed by retained binaries.
excluded: Conan 1 compatibility and binary compilation are excluded initially; not a claim of arbitrary custom server plugins.
scenarios: Upload two revisions and two binary package IDs; resolve both pinned and latest revisions.
Manifest mismatch or conflicting revision bytes fail; replicated revision order matches source.

name: Conda
protocol: Conda channel subdirectories, .conda and .tar.bz2 packages, repodata.json and compressed representations.
publish: Admin ingestion per channel/platform; extract package metadata without executing content; generate a coherent repodata generation including current_repodata where advertised.
read: conda search/install with noarch and platform packages; proxy indexes and assets as one source snapshot.
special: Preserve patched upstream repodata relationships. Local indexing uses validated package metadata. Explicit priority prevents mixing incompatible channel snapshots.
excluded: No conda-build execution or claim of arbitrary repodata patch authoring/signing extensions beyond the selected fixtures.
scenarios: Ingest noarch and platform packages in both supported containers and install a dependency chain.
Malformed archive, stale repodata-to-asset mapping and mismatched package checksum fail safely.

name: Docker / OCI
protocol: OCI Distribution 1.1 API and Docker Registry HTTP API v2 compatibility for schema-2/OCI images and multi-platform indexes.
publish: Docker push using scoped registry tokens; resumable blob upload, digest finalize and manifest/tag commit; validate referenced object closure.
read: Docker pull/tag/list behavior and manifest negotiation from local, remote pull-through and replica repositories.
special: Manifest bytes are immutable by digest; tags are conditional mutable pointers. Cross-repository mount requires source read and destination publish permission. Return accurate upload offsets and range responses.
excluded: Docker schema-1 manifests, implicit upstream push and cloud-registry administrative API emulation are excluded.
scenarios: Push/pull a multi-platform image and interrupt/resume a blob upload without corrupting digest identity.
Reject unauthorized mount, missing referenced blob and conflicting immutable manifest; proxy preserves digest bytes.

name: Git LFS
protocol: Git LFS batch API using basic HTTP transfer, SHA-256 object IDs, upload verification and range downloads.
publish: git lfs push uses batch upload actions bound to object identity and scoped credentials; verify size/hash before advertising existence.
read: git lfs pull/fetch batch requests return authorized local/proxy/replica object URLs.
policy: object-owner per LFS oid within feed
special: Object authorization must not be inferred from global blob existence; action URLs expire and cannot leak credentials across origins. Ordinary Git metadata lives in the user Git server.
excluded: LFS locking and custom transfer adapters are excluded initially; this is not a Git hosting service.
scenarios: Push then pull a large object with pinned oid; resume download from a fresh authorized batch response.
Wrong size/hash and expired action URL fail; an inaccessible deduplicated object cannot be enumerated.

name: Go modules
protocol: GOPROXY list/info/mod/zip/latest semantics with escaped paths and canonical module zip validation.
publish: Admin ingestion of immutable module version plus .mod/.info/.zip as one publish. There is no invented go publish command.
read: go mod download/build resolves public or private modules through local/remote/replica sources.
special: Preserve module path case escaping, version identity and checksums. Public clients retain their configured checksum database; private modules use documented GOPRIVATE/GONOSUMDB settings. Kuvryn Ant is not a checksum database.
excluded: No sumdb authority or VCS hosting. Never disable checksum verification globally to make the proxy work.
scenarios: Resolve a module with uppercase path escapes and a transitive dependency; repeat from warm cache/replica.
Reject invalid zip layout, conflicting immutable version or module checksum mismatch; no public fallback for private namespace.

name: Helm
protocol: Classic chart repository index.yaml/.tgz/.prov plus OCI-hosted charts through the OCI adapter.
publish: Classic charts use admin ingestion with provenance; OCI charts use helm push and the same registry credentials as helm pull.
read: helm repo add/update, pull and install for classic feeds; OCI pull/install for named chart versions.
policy: package-owner per chart; coherent classic index generation
special: Preserve chart/provenance digests and OCI media types. Classic index is adapter-generated with source-bound entries; do not reinterpret OCI manifests as generic tarballs.
excluded: No ChartMuseum-specific push API promise; chart execution is only in isolated conformance fixtures.
scenarios: Install a chart and dependency via classic feed, then push/pull the equivalent OCI chart.
Provenance/hash mismatch or tag/version conflict fails; replica retains both chart and provenance assets.

name: Hugging Face
protocol: Hub-compatible model/dataset metadata and HTTP resolve/download subset used by hf_hub_download and snapshot_download.
publish: Admin ingestion of a complete model/dataset file tree with immutable revision and optional branch/tag pointers; no Hub commit API claim.
read: Repo info/tree and HEAD/GET resolve routes support standard model/dataset downloads, ETags, revision pinning and byte ranges across local/remote/replica sources.
policy: package-owner per repo type/name; revision-bound file tree
special: Cache authorized private/gated content only under the configured upstream entitlement and feed ACL. Resolve signed external URLs internally; advertise standard HTTP transfer instead of pretending to implement Xet.
excluded: Hub social/inference/training/Spaces APIs, Git pushes, native Xet CAS and general Hub upload APIs are excluded. Models and datasets remain in scope.
scenarios: snapshot_download a versioned multi-file model and dataset, then resume a large file from replica while source is offline.
Missing file or unauthorized gated content prevents complete snapshot success; no cross-credential cache disclosure.

name: Maven
protocol: Maven2 repository layout with POMs, maven-metadata.xml, release and timestamped snapshot assets and checksums.
publish: Maven deploy and Gradle maven-publish upload a staged coordinate set; commit a version/index generation only after required metadata/assets validate.
read: Maven/Gradle resolve dependencies and plugins using local/remote/replica feeds and release/snapshot policy.
policy: package-owner per groupId/artifactId; version-bound snapshot generation
special: Preserve client-required legacy checksum files alongside internal SHA-256; checksum compatibility is not a cryptographic trust upgrade. Metadata update races use generation checks.
excluded: No Maven Central account/staging API clone or build execution. Partial deployment must not look complete.
scenarios: Deploy release and two timestamped snapshots, then resolve from Maven and Gradle with checksums.
Concurrent metadata update cannot lose a version; incomplete deployment and bad checksum remain invisible.

name: npm
protocol: npm registry packuments, scoped packages, tarball attachments, dist-tags, publish/unpublish subset and token auth.
publish: npm publish validates package metadata/tarball digest and atomically commits a version. Dist-tag changes and deletion require separate permissions/policy.
read: npm install/view/dist-tag behavior with local/remote/replica packuments; rewrite tarball URLs to authorized feed assets.
special: Return integrity metadata matching exact tarball bytes; serialize mutable tag/packument changes. Login/bootstrap provides a machine token compatible with npm configuration, not browser SSO at registry routes.
excluded: Public npm organization/billing APIs, audit advisory service emulation and upstream publishing are excluded.
scenarios: Publish scoped package, move a dist-tag and install a lockfile from cache and replica.
Private name cannot fall through upstream; conflicting version/tarball integrity and unauthorized unpublish fail.

name: NuGet / Chocolatey
protocol: NuGet v3 service index/registration/flat-container/search/publish plus v2 OData package discovery/download/publish needed by Chocolatey.
publish: dotnet nuget push and Chocolatey push accept nupkg; symbol ingestion supports snupkg and a documented legacy symbols.nupkg path, validating identity/PDB inventory.
read: dotnet restore and choco install consume packages; symbol lookup/download is separately exercised with Windows debugging tooling.
special: Normalize versions consistently across v2/v3; API keys and download auth share scopes. Symbol assets retain PDB identifiers, checksums and access policy; package scripts are never run on the server.
excluded: NuGet.org account/gallery APIs and executing Chocolatey scripts server-side are excluded. Symbol workflow requires Windows client evidence before claim.
scenarios: Push/restore package through v3, install via v2 Chocolatey, and retrieve matching symbols.
Mismatched symbol identity, unauthorized package/symbol request and version-normalization collision fail.

name: OCI artifacts
protocol: OCI Distribution 1.1 non-container artifacts with subject/referrers discovery and media-type preservation.
publish: ORAS push/attach publishes manifests and referenced blobs; validate subject access and closure through the shared OCI core.
read: ORAS pull/discover/copy consumes artifacts and referrers from local/remote/replica repositories.
policy: package-owner per OCI repository; digest-bound subject graph
special: Referrers are indexed without rewriting manifest bytes. GC and replication account for subject/referrer relationships. Distinguish artifact conformance from image conformance.
excluded: No server-side execution of artifacts or assertion that stored attestations are trusted without external verification.
scenarios: Attach an artifact to an image digest, discover and pull it, then verify replica subject graph.
Cross-scope subject access fails; deleting a subject cannot silently orphan protected retained attachments.

name: Eclipse p2
protocol: p2 metadata/artifact repositories, XML/JAR index representations, composite repository descriptors and installable units.
publish: Admin ingestion of a validated p2 repository or IU/artifact bundle; generate a consistent repository snapshot without changing signed JAR bytes.
read: p2 director installs a selected IU and dependencies from local, remote mirror/cache or replica snapshots.
special: Composite child references are scoped and materialized for offline full seed; retain classifier/id/version relationships. Preserve upstream signed artifacts and compressed index semantics.
excluded: Legacy Pack200 transformation, general Eclipse marketplace APIs and building plugins are excluded initially; reject fixtures requiring unimplemented transforms.
scenarios: Install an IU with dependencies using p2 director and repeat from seeded offline replica.
Broken child reference, unsigned substitution for a signed artifact or incomplete IU closure fails validation.

name: Pub / Flutter
protocol: Hosted Pub Repository Specification v2 with package/version metadata, archives, archive hashes and staged publish.
publish: dart pub publish to publish_to uses token auth and upload/finalize behavior; validate pubspec and archive before visibility.
read: dart pub get and flutter pub get resolve packages from local, remote and replica hosted repositories.
special: Preserve archive SHA-256 and retraction/discontinuation metadata; do not silently replace a published version. Credentials remain tied to hosted origin.
excluded: Pub.dev social/scoring/account APIs and server-side package execution are excluded.
scenarios: Publish a dependency chain and resolve through Dart and Flutter with lockfile hashes.
Failed finalize, archive tampering and unauthorized token reuse cannot produce installable content.

name: PyPI
protocol: Simple Repository API HTML and JSON representations, normalized project names, wheel/sdist files, hashes, yanked and requires-python metadata.
publish: Twine multipart uploads validate distribution filenames/project/version and payload integrity; atomically add the release file set with provenance.
read: pip install/download from local/remote/replica Simple endpoints; serve metadata sidecars when advertised.
special: Rewrite file URLs while preserving hashes and sidecar relationships; authorization precedes enumeration. Distinct normalized names cannot bypass ownership.
excluded: PyPI account/UI/XML-RPC emulation and building sdists on the server are excluded.
scenarios: Upload wheel and sdist, then pip install with hashes and Python-version filtering from replica.
Reject normalized-name conflict, hash mismatch and unauthorized upload; yanked metadata survives replication.

name: R / CRAN
protocol: CRAN-style source and Windows/macOS binary repository layouts with PACKAGES, PACKAGES.gz and PACKAGES.rds.
publish: Admin ingestion of source/binary packages into explicit R-version/platform channels; generate package indexes after metadata validation.
read: R available.packages/install.packages uses local, remote and replica indexes and package archives.
special: Keep source/binary identities distinct and preserve dependencies/MD5 metadata alongside internal SHA-256. Binary evidence must run on its native platform.
excluded: CRAN submission/review services and server-side R package builds or install hooks are excluded.
scenarios: Install source plus a dependency on Linux and binary fixtures on Windows/macOS.
Wrong R/platform placement or corrupt archive is rejected; index points only to committed assets.

name: Raw
protocol: HTTP GET/HEAD/PUT/DELETE with range and conditional request semantics; management browse/search API.
publish: PUT streams one path to its uniquely selected local source; optional expected SHA-256/size; immutable by default, overwrite requires policy and precondition.
read: GET/HEAD, byte ranges, conditional retrieval and authorized listing for local/remote/replica paths.
special: Normalize once and reject traversal/ambiguous encodings; distinguish content type from execution. Remote URLs use configured base mapping, never arbitrary client-directed proxy targets.
excluded: No WebDAV, executable directory listing, archive expansion or claim that raw file storage constitutes another format.
scenarios: PUT a large file, GET a range, HEAD/ETag revalidate and repeat through a replica.
Reject traversal, digest mismatch and concurrent conflicting immutable PUT; cancelled upload remains invisible.

name: RubyGems
protocol: Gem push/download plus RubyGems indexes and Bundler compact-index dependency resolution.
publish: gem push publishes validated gem metadata/archive under API-key authorization; yank is a policy-controlled metadata change.
read: gem install and bundle install use compact and legacy dependency/index representations from local, remote and replica.
special: Preserve platform-specific versions and immutable gem bytes; index generation/yank changes are atomic. Never execute gemspec/Ruby hooks while indexing uploads.
excluded: RubyGems.org account/organization APIs and server-side native extension builds are excluded.
scenarios: Push platform variants and install a locked dependency set with gem/Bundler.
Yanked release handling remains consistent; malformed archive or conflicting version bytes fail.

name: Rust / Cargo
protocol: Cargo alternate-registry Web API, sparse HTTP index and Git index transport; crate archives and checksums.
publish: cargo publish commits crate bytes and index metadata, with scoped registry token and owner policy. Yank/unyank mutates availability, not crate bytes.
read: cargo fetch/build consumes both sparse and Git index configurations from local/remote/replica feeds.
special: Index config points to authorized crate/download/API routes; keep dependency features/schema fields. Git index is generated protocol state, not arbitrary user repository hosting.
excluded: Public crates.io account/team/search ranking behavior and compiling crates server-side are excluded.
scenarios: Publish and fetch a dependency chain with sparse and Git indexes, then verify checksum-preserving replica.
Invalid checksum, ambiguous crate normalization or unauthorized yank cannot corrupt index state.

name: Swift Package Manager
protocol: Swift package registry protocol v1, scoped identities, releases, manifests and source archives.
publish: Swift registry publish uses authenticated immutable version upload and validates archive/checksum/manifest inventory; preserve signatures where supplied.
read: Swift package resolve/download via a configured registry across local/remote/replica sources.
special: Use protocol-supported authentication and retain signing/fingerprint metadata; run macOS and Linux clients against the selected SDK. Source archives are data, not server-executed code.
excluded: General Git hosting and promising compatibility with arbitrary future registry protocol extensions are excluded.
scenarios: Publish and resolve a scoped package with manifest/archive checksums on selected Swift clients.
Identity mismatch, corrupt archive and signer/fingerprint mismatch have explicit failures; replica preserves metadata.

name: Terraform
protocol: Terraform provider and module registry protocols with host service discovery, versions, provider platform downloads and module source retrieval.
publish: Admin ingestion of provider binaries/checksums/signatures and module archives; validate namespace/name/provider/version/platform coordinates.
read: terraform init resolves provider and module dependencies through local/remote/replica registry endpoints.
policy: package-owner per provider or module address
special: Feed-specific hostname binds discovery and credentials. Preserve provider signing material; module download references resolve to authorized immutable archives. Full offline seeds require materialized referenced sources.
excluded: Terraform Cloud workspace/state/run APIs and executing providers/modules server-side are excluded.
scenarios: Initialize a configuration with one provider and one module for two platforms, including checksum/signature files.
Reject substituted provider bytes, incorrect signing metadata or incomplete module closure; replica works offline.

name: Yum / RPM
protocol: RPM-MD repomd.xml and primary/filelists/other metadata with repository/package signing and compressed indexes.
publish: Admin ingestion of RPMs by repository/architecture; generate and sign a coherent RPM-MD snapshot; retain existing package signatures.
read: DNF and yum-compatible invocation consume local/remote/replica repositories; provide explicitly advertised auxiliary metadata consistently.
special: Preserve updateinfo/comps and module metadata when present in mirrored snapshots; local module metadata can be ingested/validated rather than synthesized. Never mix a signed index from one generation with another generation’s bytes.
excluded: RPM build execution and automatic construction of distro modular streams are excluded; no legacy yum2 client claim.
scenarios: Ingest signed RPMs, refresh metadata and install a dependency using DNF/yum-compatible client flow.
Tampered repomd or package signature fails; concurrent snapshot updates and replicas keep reference integrity.
